memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then Joshua son of Nun secretly sent two spies from Shittim. "Go, look over the land," he said, "especially Jericho." So they went and entered the house of a prostitute named Rahab and stayed there. — Josh 2:1 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Joshua had just been told three times to be strong and courageous, and God had promised to give Israel the land. So why send spies at all? Because trusting God does not mean acting foolishly. Faith and wise planning are not opposites. Joshua believed the promise, and he also prepared carefully. We can hold both in our hands.

Notice where the spies end up — in the house of Rahab, a woman the text plainly calls a prostitute. Scripture does not hide her past or dress it up. And yet this is exactly where God's grace is about to shine. God has a way of working through people the world writes off. The most unlikely house in Jericho becomes the safest place in the city.

If you have ever felt disqualified by your past, take heart. God is not looking for people with spotless records; He is looking for people who will trust Him. Rahab's story is proof that grace reaches into the places we would never expect.

Later, the New Testament names Rahab among the heroes of faith (Heb 11:31) and even in the family line of Jesus Himself (Matt 1:5). The Saviour was not ashamed to be born from a line that included her — and He is not ashamed of you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you see planning and trusting God as opposites, or as partners?
2. Have you ever felt too "disqualified" for God to use you?
3. How does it encourage you that Rahab appears in Jesus' family line?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that Your grace reaches the unlikely and the overlooked. Help me trust You wisely and never feel too far gone for Your mercy. Amen.
